title: DC-area forecast: Heat and humidity slowly step back this week as storm chances fluctuate
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: Starting in the 70s this morning with clouds, a few showers, and maybe a rumble of thunder. Increasing sun by late morning or early afternoon as highs head for the mid-80s to near 90. Scattered showers and storms are possible by late afternoon.

What’s next? We slowly downshift humidity tomorrow and Thursday with somewhat lower storm chances. Friday is an iffy forecast before a more confidently cooler and less humid Saturday.

Today’s daily digit — 5/10: We know some of you are tough graders, but hopefully you'll agree that today's slight drop in temperatures and humidity is a digit-boosting step in the right direction. | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.

Forecast in detail

Today (Tuesday): Clouds are our first order of business this morning with a few showers and maybe a rumble of thunder. Turning partly to mostly sunny by late morning or early afternoon, although wildfire smoke adds a bit of haze, with highs in the mid-80s to near 90 and light winds from the west. Feeling a touch less humid with dew points in the mid-60s to near 70. Scattered showers and storms are possible by late afternoon, especially after 3 p.m. A couple of storms could have damaging winds. Confidence: Medium

Tonight: Partly to mostly cloudy with scattered showers and storms possible during the evening or overnight. Lows toward dawn in the upper 60s to mid-70s with moderate mugginess. Light winds continue from the west at 5 to 10 mph. Confidence: Medium

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow (Wednesday): Partly sunny, moderately muggy, and highs mainly in the mid- to upper 80s. Less moisture in the atmosphere should limit chances for showers and storms, but a couple could still pop up in the afternoon or evening. We may also still have a bit of smoky haze in our skies. Winds are light and variable in direction. Confidence: Medium

Tomorrow night: Partly to mostly cloudy with the chance of isolated to scattered showers and storms lingering into the evening. Still fairly muggy with lows in the upper 60s to mid-70s. Confidence: Medium

Our morning forecast email is back! It's included with every level of support — from Free to Sustainer — delivered 7 days a week. Sign up at: capitalweather.com/support-us

A look ahead

Thursday should begin the process of further lowering humidity as temperatures hit highs in the upper 80s to near 90 under partly sunny skies. There is still a chance for an isolated shower or storm though. Thursday night is partly cloudy with lows in the upper 60s to low 70s. Confidence: Medium-High

Friday has a chance to be our best day of the workweek with highs in the 80s, noticeably lower humidity, and a slim shower chance – however, that's only if a cold front slips far enough to our south. Friday night is partly cloudy and more confidently comfortable with lower humidity and 60s for lows. Confidence: Low-Medium

The upcoming weekend looks to start nice on Saturday with mostly sunny skies, low humidity, and highs in the low to mid-80s. Sunday could trend a touch warmer and more humid with highs aiming for the mid- to upper 80s under partly sunny skies. A shower and storm chance could return late Sunday, but we'll have to see how things look as we get closer. Partly cloudy Saturday night with lows in the 60s again. Confidence: Medium

Next week looks like near-normal August weather with partly sunny days, highs mostly in the 80s, moderate humidity, and occasional thunderstorm chances.

DC weather history for August 11

Torrential rains in 1928 set a daily record and caused widespread flooding and rescues, while in 1984 another deluge produced extreme local totals—highlighting how dramatically rainfall can vary across short distances.
